title: If and When
description: Say what you'll do if it rains and when you get paid, wish for what isn't, and hedge like a Cairene: لو with a past verb and a future result, لما for 'when', يا ريت and نفسي for wishes, and على حسب for everything else.
approach: Pattern noticing from street interviews — Easy Arabic's 'what would you do if…' answers supply the لو… هـ frame; learners sort real from unreal, then answer the same questions themselves.
unlock_condition: Answer three 'what if' questions with a correct لو… هـ sentence each; ≥8/10 on the if / when sorting quiz
can_do: Say what you would do if something happened
Express a wish and hedge an answer

grammar.title: لو + past, result in the future; لما for 'when'
grammar.explanation: A real condition in Egyptian puts the if-clause in the past or present and the result in the future or as a command: لو شفته، هقوله (if I see him, I'll tell him); لو عندك وقت، تعالى (if you have time, come). لو is the everyday 'if'; إذا means the same and sounds a touch more careful. For an unreal wish or a might-have-been, add كان: لو كان معايا فلوس، كنت اشتريت عربية (if I had money, I'd have bought a car) — recognise this now, produce it later. لما is 'when' for a time you are sure of, past or future: لما أرجع هكلمك (when I get back I'll call you). It is never a question word — that is إمتى. Trap: عندما and بينما are MSA and fail the detector.

examples.english: If it rains, we won't go out
If you have time, come with us
When I arrive I'll send you a message
If I were you, I would have agreed
If the train is late, I'll take a bus

culture.title: The polite hypothetical
culture.note: Egyptians soften almost everything with a condition or a wish. An invitation is لو فاضي، تعالى (if you're free, come) — leaving you an exit; a request is لو سمحت (if you'd allow); a refusal is إن شاء الله with a tilt of the head, which everyone understands as 'probably not'. Answers to 'when?' come as على حسب (it depends) or ربنا يسهل (God will make it easy), which are not evasions but good manners: promising a time you might miss is worse than not promising. Wishes are said out loud — يا ريت (if only), نفسي (I'd love to) — and the listener replies يا رب (please God) or ربنا يحققلك (may God grant it).

phrases.english: If you're free, come have dinner with us
God will make it easy (we'll see)
Please God (in reply to a wish)

vocabulary.teaching_note: The everyday 'if', real or unreal. Followed by a past or present verb, or by عند / معا: لو عندك، لو معاك. You already know it fossilised in لو سمحت (if you'd allow = please). Trap: إن + verb is MSA in this sense.
vocabulary.image_scene: A weather forecast icon split between sun and rain, a question mark in the middle.

example.english: If you come early we'll have lunch together

vocabulary.video_hint: A conditional answer in an interview: لو… هـ…

vocabulary.english: if I were / if I had (unreal if)
vocabulary.teaching_note: لو plus كان turns the condition unreal: لو كنت مكانك (if I were you), لو كنت عارف (if I had known). The result then also takes كان: كنت قلتلك (I would have told you). Learn the frame لو كنت مكانك as one chunk — it starts half of all advice in Cairo.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman imagining herself in a friend's shoes, a dashed outline of herself standing in the friend's place.

example.english: If I were you, I'd have refused

vocabulary.video_hint: Advice framed with لو كنت مكانك; a regret with لو كنت عارف.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Time, past or future, that you are sure of: لما وصلت (when I arrived), لما أخلص (when I finish). Trap 1: it is not the question word — إمتى asks 'when?'. Trap 2: عندما is MSA and fails the detector. Also 'until' in لما تيجي (wait till you come).
vocabulary.image_scene: A clock with an arrow to a door opening, a person stepping in.

example.english: When I finish work I'll call you

vocabulary.video_hint: A plan sequenced with لما: لما أرجع / لما نوصل.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The wish word. Alone it is 'I wish!' as an answer; before a sentence it is 'if only': يا ريت أقدر (if only I could). Takes a pronoun: يا ريتك (I wish you…), يا ريتني. Trap: ليت is its MSA ancestor — never said.
vocabulary.image_scene: A girl looking up at a shooting star with her hands clasped.

example.english: I wish I could travel this summer

vocabulary.video_hint: A wish voiced in an interview: يا ريت… ; يا ريت! as a reply.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Possibility and permission in one word. ممكن؟ (may I?), ممكن أساعدك (can I help you), مش ممكن (impossible / no way), ممكن يمطر (it might rain). Invariable — no endings. The polite request opener of the whole country.
vocabulary.image_scene: A hand raised politely, a half-open door beyond it.

example.english: We can meet tomorrow if you're free

vocabulary.video_hint: ممكن opening a request or a hedge: ممكن أسأل؟ / ممكن يحصل.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Draws the conclusion of a condition: لو مش جاي، يبقى نلغي (if you're not coming, then we cancel). Literally 'it becomes'. Also the future of 'to be': هيبقى (it will be). Trap: بعدين is 'then' in time; يبقى is 'then' in logic.
vocabulary.image_scene: A flowchart arrow leading from a question box to a green decision box.

example.english: The weather's nice? Then let's go out

vocabulary.video_hint: A conclusion drawn with يبقى… after a condition.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Warning shape: اسرع وإلا هتتأخر (hurry, otherwise you'll be late). Same sound as ولا (or) in questions — شاي ولا قهوة؟ — so the meaning comes from position: at the start of the second clause it is 'otherwise'. غير كده (other than that) does the same job.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man pointing at a clock with a raised eyebrow, a bus pulling away outside.

example.english: Take an umbrella, otherwise you'll get wet

vocabulary.video_hint: A warning with وإلا…; advice ending in غير كده.

vocabulary.english: in case / as a precaution / spare
vocabulary.teaching_note: How Egyptian says 'just in case': خد فلوس احتياطي (take money in case). Also 'spare' as an adjective: مفتاح احتياطي (spare key). Precaution is the whole idea — لو حصل حاجة (if something happens) is the longer way to say it.
vocabulary.image_scene: An umbrella tucked into a bag on a sunny day.

example.arabic: خد جاكيت احتياطي، الجو بيبرد بالليل
example.transliteration: khud jakitt iḥtiyaaṭi, ig-gaww biyibrad bil-leel
example.english: Take a jacket in case, it gets cold at night

vocabulary.video_hint: Packing or planning advice with احتياطي / لو حصل حاجة.

vocabulary.teaching_note: كان plus the هـ future gives 'was going to / would': كنت هروح (I was going to go), كان هيكلمك (he was going to call you). This is how Egyptian says 'would' in a polite or unreal sense: كنت هقول إن… (I would say that…). Conjugate كان, keep هـ.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man with his coat half on, looking at his ringing phone, the door ajar.

example.english: I was going to call you but I forgot

vocabulary.video_hint: A plan that didn't happen: كنت هـ… بس…

vocabulary.teaching_note: The Egyptian 'would have… by now': كان زمانه وصل (he'd have arrived by now), كان زمانك خلصت (you'd have finished by now). Put the pronoun on زمان. Literally 'it was time'. Pure dialect — there is nothing like it in MSA.
vocabulary.image_scene: An empty chair at a table with a place set, a clock showing late.

example.arabic: لو ركبنا المترو، كان زماننا وصلنا
example.transliteration: law rikibna l-metro, kaan zamaanna wṣilna
example.english: If we'd taken the metro, we'd have arrived by now

vocabulary.video_hint: A regret with كان زمان… after a bad choice.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The most useful hedge in the language. Alone: على حسب (it depends). With what it depends on: على حسب الجو (depending on the weather), على حسب الوقت. Also just حسب. Trap: يعتمد على is MSA and sounds like a news anchor.
vocabulary.image_scene: A pair of scales with a sun on one pan and a cloud on the other.

example.english: When will you come? Depends on the traffic

vocabulary.video_hint: An interview answer beginning على حسب…

vocabulary.teaching_note: فرصة كويسة (a good chance), لو لقيت فرصة (if I get a chance), فرصة سعيدة (pleased to meet you — literally 'a happy chance', said on parting). Plural فرص.
vocabulary.image_scene: An open door with light streaming through, a person about to step in.

example.arabic: لو جات فرصة هسافر على طول
example.transliteration: law gaat furṣa hasaafir ʿala ṭuul
example.english: If a chance comes I'll travel right away

vocabulary.video_hint: Someone talking about an opportunity: فرصة / لو جات الفرصة.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The other 'if' — interchangeable with لو for real conditions, slightly more careful in tone. Also used for 'whether' after asking: سألني إذا كنت جاي (he asked me whether I was coming). Note the Cairo pronunciation: iza, with a z.
vocabulary.image_scene: Two doors side by side, one labelled with a sun, one with a cloud.

example.english: If the weather's nice, we'll go to the sea

vocabulary.video_hint: إذا beginning a condition or a reported question.

vocabulary.teaching_note: كل (every) plus ما: كل ما أشوفه (every time I see him). Also 'the more': كل ما تذاكر أكتر، كل ما تفهم أكتر (the more you study, the more you understand). Sister of أول ما and طول ما.
vocabulary.image_scene: A calendar with the same small icon repeated on every day.

example.arabic: كل ما أروح مصر بزور خان الخليلي
example.transliteration: kull ma aruuḥ maṣr bazuur khaan il-khaliili
example.english: Whenever I go to Egypt I visit Khan el-Khalili

vocabulary.video_hint: A habit framed with كل ما…

vocabulary.teaching_note: طول (length) plus ما: طول ما إنت هنا (as long as you're here). Sets a condition that lasts. Also طول الوقت (all the time) and على طول (straight / always) share the root.
vocabulary.image_scene: A long road with a person walking and a companion beside them all the way.

example.arabic: طول ما إنت معايا مش خايف
example.transliteration: ṭuul ma nta maʿaaya mish khaayif
example.english: As long as you're with me I'm not afraid

vocabulary.video_hint: A reassurance or condition with طول ما…

vocabulary.teaching_note: A noun (possibility) used as a hedge: احتمال أجي (I might come), احتمال كبير (very likely), مفيش احتمال (no chance). Softer than أكيد, firmer than يمكن.
vocabulary.image_scene: A weather dial pointing between 'sunny' and 'rain'.

example.english: I might be a bit late

vocabulary.video_hint: A hedged plan: احتمال… in a phone call or interview.

vocabulary.english: I'd love to / I really want to
vocabulary.teaching_note: Literally 'my self' — نفسي أسافر (I'd love to travel), نفسي في كوباية شاي (I'm craving a cup of tea). Change the pronoun: نفسك، نفسه، نفسها. Stronger and dreamier than عايز. Trap: the same word means 'myself' in ضحكت على نفسي.
vocabulary.image_scene: A young man gazing at a travel poster of the sea with a dreamy smile.

example.english: I'd love to see the pyramids at night

vocabulary.video_hint: A wish voiced with نفسي… in a vlog or interview.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The plain 'maybe' of Cairo: يمكن أجي (maybe I'll come), يمكن (maybe — as a whole answer). Next to it sits جايز (possibly) and احتمال. Trap: ربما is written Arabic.
vocabulary.image_scene: A person tilting a hand side to side in a 'maybe' gesture.

example.english: Maybe we'll go to Alexandria tomorrow

vocabulary.video_hint: يمكن as a hedge before a plan; يمكن alone as an answer.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: هتعمل إيه لو كسبت مليون جنيه؟
dialogue.transliteration: hatiʿmil eeh law kisibt milyoon gineeh?
dialogue.english: What would you do if you won a million pounds?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: لو كسبت مليون، هسافر على طول. نفسي أشوف اليابان.
dialogue.transliteration: law kisibt milyoon, hasaafir ʿala ṭuul. nifsi ashuuf il-yabaan.
dialogue.english: If I won a million, I'd travel right away. I'd love to see Japan.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.english: I wish! And when you come back?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.english: It depends. Maybe I'd open a restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: لو كنت مكانك، كنت اشتريت شقة الأول.
dialogue.transliteration: law kunt makaanik, kunt ishtareet shaʾʾa l-awwil.
dialogue.english: If I were you, I'd have bought a flat first.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: معاكي حق. يبقى شقة الأول، وبعدين المطعم.
dialogue.transliteration: maʿaaki ḥaʾʾ. yibʾa shaʾʾa l-awwil, wi-baʿdeen il-maṭʿam.
dialogue.english: You're right. Then a flat first, and the restaurant after.

sound_spotlight.sound: ذ said as z in إذا
sound_spotlight.explanation: In learned words the Cairo ذ becomes a plain z, never the th of MSA. In everyday inherited words it is d instead: ده، دي، دهب.

sound_spotlight.sound: The helping vowel before a cluster
sound_spotlight.example: لو كنت مكانك → law kunt-i makaanak
sound_spotlight.explanation: When three consonants pile up across words, a tiny i slips in: kunt makaanak sounds like kunti makaanak. Do not write it, do say it.
Cairo's future marker is a light h, never the throaty ḥ. You will hear حـ (ḥaruuḥ) from Alexandrians and in older texts — understand it, but say هـ.

lesson_sequence.detail: Five short interview answers to 'what would you do if…?' play once each. Just listen for لو and what follows it.
Second pass with transcripts: sort each answer — plain لو + هـ (real) or لو كان… كان (unreal). The pattern surfaces without a rule being stated.
The conditional and لما note, examples from the clips, with a drag-the-result exercise.
The 18 words with audio; the hedges (على حسب، احتمال، يمكن، إن شاء الله) grouped so their strength can be compared.
Record your own answers to the five interview questions. The app checks each for لو plus a هـ result.
Three يا ريت / نفسي wishes, spoken; the app plays back a native يا رب after each.
Words counter rolls up. Nudge: next time you decline something, try لو فاضي بكرة… instead of no.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Invite someone conditionally today: لو فاضي، تعالى… — and accept whatever they answer.
real_world_prompts.context: Lesson-complete screen. Activates لو and the polite invitation frame.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Say one wish out loud in Egyptian tonight: يا ريت… or نفسي…
real_world_prompts.context: Evening notification. Activates the wish words.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Ask your tutor لو كنت مكاني، كنت عملت إيه؟ about a real decision you're facing.
real_world_prompts.context: Tutor prompt. Elicits the unreal conditional for recognition.
